Ada AD102; dense tensor peaks at the 2.73 GHz this card holds under a bf16 GEMM - not the 2.52 GHz rated boost clock NVIDIA's sheet figures are computed at. GPU Boost clears the rated clock on a GeForce part so the sheet peak is no speed-of-light bound: measured steady 2730 MHz at 388 W / 50 C under the 450 W cap. The MMA ladder measured on this card at 8192^3: bf16 164.5 TFLOPs (471 FLOP/SM/clk), fp8_e4m3 329.6 (943), int8 580.7 (1662) - the hardware's rates are 512 : 1024 : 2048 FLOP/SM/clk, so int8 is 4x bf16 HERE where every datacenter row has it at 2x. That is the GeForce FP32-accumulate halving: int8 accumulates in int32 and is not halved; fp16/bf16 with FP32 accumulate are. Which makes the fp16/bf16 column the FP32-ACCUMULATE rate - what every kernel measured here runs (cuBLAS and Triton both default to it). The same cuBLAS call accumulating in fp16 measured 238.5 TFLOPs, 133% of this column, on the 1024 FLOP/SM/clk path the sheet's 330.3 names: a row measured on an fp16-accumulating kernel is the one case this column understates and needs its own peak rather than a widened one. no NVLink - PCIe Gen4 x16 -> 32 GB/s/dir intra-node; consumer boxes have no RDMA - typical 100 GbE -> 12.5 GB/s/dir cross-node

CANN SoC profile Ascend910_9362.ini and torch_npu device properties, both read on the box 2026-11-14, agree on the per-die physics: cube_core_cnt=20, vector_core_cnt=40, cube 16x16x16 (= 8192 FLOP/cycle), cube_freq=1500 MHz nominal, L2 168 MiB. 20 x 8192 x 1500 MHz = 245.76 TFLOPs, which a bf16 GEMM CLEARS: 248.4 TFLOPs measured at 4096^3, reproducibly (best and median within 0.1), implying 1516 MHz sustained. So the bf16/fp16 cell is 20 x 8192 x 1516 MHz = 248.4 - the rate at the clock the part actually holds under tensor-core work, which is what a roofline needs (the RTX-4090 row's case). int8 is the cube's 2x rate, 496.8; measured 392.5 TOPs = 79% of it, and int8 must exceed 1x since the measurement exceeds the bf16 cell. This REPLACES 376/752/94, which came from a third-party note claiming 24 cube cores, 48 vector cores and 192 MB L2 - all three wrong for this chip. fp32 is the cube's quarter rate and is MEASURED: 63.3 TFLOPs at 4096^3, which the former 62.1 cell (the same quarter rate at bf16's 1516 MHz) did not bound. The two clocks differ because the parts boost differently under different work - an fp32 GEMM implies 1545 MHz against bf16's 1516 - so each column states its own measured rate rather than one clock's. HBM bandwidth 1600 GB/s is the vendor figure, NOT confirmed by CANN; a device-to-device copy reached 1262 GB/s (79%), so it stands as a bound. No FP8/FP4 MMA: those columns are empty on purpose. HBM 65536 MiB per die (npu-smi -t memory; torch_npu reports 61.27 GiB usable). One row is ONE DIE: npu-smi shows 8 packages x 2 chips = 16 devices, and CANN / torch_npu / HCCL / vLLM-Ascend expose each die as its own device, so a rank is a die. Atlas 800T A3 node = 16 dies; the scale-up link is HCCS: npu-smi -t topo shows every die reaching every other over HCCS_SW, with dies paired 0-1, 2-3, ... over a faster package-internal SIO link, MEASURED. The 196 GB/s per-direction cell BOUNDS what HCCL reached: 186.4 GB/s bus bandwidth on 16 dies and 132.8 on a pure-HCCS group of 8 (one die per package), at 128 MiB payloads, 2026-11-15. Bus not algorithm bandwidth - the ring's share of the payload (comm_volume.ring_factor) is what crosses the link. A group taking both dies of a package reads higher (213.2 on dies 0-7) because part of that traffic rides SIO, not HCCS. The per-link decomposition (7 links x 28 GB/s) is a vendor constant this box cannot confirm - the hccs-bw counter reports utilisation, not the peak. The RDMA cells are EMPTY. The NIC is stated as a 200 Gbps RoCE v2 port per die (25 GB/s/dir at line rate), but this node's RoCE ports are not in service - hccn_tool reports 'Speed: Unknown!', 'link status: DOWN' and no preset IP - so the rate cannot be read off the hardware here and no cross-node collective can be run to bound it; a nameplate nothing on this row has checked is left out rather than priced. Every measurement on this row is intra-node. SUPERNODE: npu-smi -t spod-info reports Super Pod Size 384 PACKAGES (= 768 dies) and Super Pod ID 2 on these five hosts, whose Server Index runs 20-24 of a 0-based 0..47 (idx 47 answers hccs_ping, 48 is silent) - so ranks_per_scaleup_domain is 768 while gpus_per_node stays 16, the chassis. Crossing chassis inside it is NOT scale-out: RoCE is DOWN with link-up-count 0 and never carried any of this, while hccn_tool -hccs_ping reaches a peer die in 5.6-8.7us over Lingqu (UB). MEASURED 2026-11-20 at 512 MiB bf16, p50 of the group, two nodes agreeing to 0.2%: all_reduce 178.8 GB/s on 16 dies of one chassis, 174.5 GB/s on 32 dies across two (0.98x), 189.7 GB/s on 8+8; all_to_all 112.3 / 106.8 / 124.7 GB/s the same three ways. The one-chassis figure agrees with the out-of-band 176.7 GB/s to 1.2%. So a group that crosses machines inside the supernode is priced on the scale-up cell, not the RDMA one; that cell stays the nominal 7x28, as every other row states nominal and lets the walk and the corpus carry efficiency. The RDMA cells on this row (rdma_gbps and rdma_hop_latency_us) are both EMPTY and for the same reason: this node's RoCE ports have never carried anything (hccn_tool reports link status DOWN and a link-up count of 0), so neither a rate nor a hop latency can be read off this hardware. They would be reached only by a group wider than the 768-die scale-up domain, or by a disaggregated handoff between clusters that do not fit one such domain -- inside it, traffic crosses Lingqu (UB) and is priced on the scale-up cells, which ARE measured. A deployment that does leave the supernode is refused with the column named instead of priced on an unchecked nameplate; a KV handoff there is priced once the request states the link (kv_transfer_bw_gbps). The 5.6-8.7 us this cluster does show between chassis is a scale-up ping and belongs to no RDMA cell.
